compensating.why: hop 4 gives the parameters for the class itself
hop 2 tests the class the parameters are for
hop 3 checks the count of a Collection by the class the parameters are for

edits.old:
if (Map.class.isAssignableFrom(raw)) return factory.constructMapType((Class<Map<?,?>>) raw, parameterTypes[0], parameterTypes[1]);
        if (Collection.class.isAssignableFrom(raw)) return factory.constructCollectionType((Class<Collection<?>>) raw, parameterTypes[0]);

ownership_reason: Only the gold constructs the type of a non-array class: a map type for a Map class, a collection type for a Collection class, a simple type otherwise. Hops 1 and 4 pass the class and its parameters along unchanged; hop 2 constructs array types only and passes every other class on unchanged; hop 3 only checks the number of parameters of a Map or Collection class and passes the class on unchanged. Once the gold has built a SimpleType for ArrayList, a CollectionType can appear only if a caller replaces the gold's result or constructs the type itself. The gold's javadoc promises the type 'as the type factory resolves the class when it is declared with those parameters'; the factory resolves a Collection class declared with type parameters as a CollectionType. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the intact sibling TypeFactory._fromParameterizedClass (the TypeParser path, a class plus parameter types) gives a Map class MapType.construct, a Collection class CollectionType.construct and any other class constructSimpleType, as do TypeFactory._fromParamType and _fromClass in production; TestTypeFactory::testCollections and ::testCanonicalNames pass on the variant (ArrayList and ArrayList<String> resolve to CollectionType), as do the chain-path tests TestWithGenerics::testWrapperWithExplicitType and TestTypedContainerSerialization::testIssue329.
